output.summary: KEP-4322 proposes a universal ClusterProfile API as a standard cluster inventory, defining a common status-reporting interface that multiple multi-cluster management implementations can support. The KEP is currently provisional at alpha stage.
output.rationale: There is no standard way to access a cluster inventory, even though most multi-cluster management solutions include one. Consumers such as schedulers, GitOps tools, and operators must currently learn each project's own cluster APIs. The KEP proposes a shared interface for discovering clusters, their properties, and status, while allowing multiple implementations. The status is provisional, so the design is still a proposal and not yet an accepted decision.

alternatives.option: Each multi-cluster project keeps its own cluster API and consumers adapt to each one
alternatives.why_not: The readme says consumers 'either need to build the cluster concept by themselves or understand APIs representing a cluster from each cluster management project', which the proposed common API is meant to avoid.

alternatives.option: Provide a standard reference implementation of the cluster inventory
alternatives.why_not: This is listed as a non-goal: 'Provide a standard reference implementation.'

alternatives.option: Define the Consumer registration API as part of this KEP
alternatives.why_not: This is listed as a non-goal: 'Define the Consumer registration API'.

evidence.quote: there is not a standard way to access such an inventory; as we see more and more users embrace the cloud-native approach
The objective is to establish a shared interface for cluster inventory, defining a standard for status reporting while allowing for multiple implementations.
GitOps tools (ArgoCD, flux etc) are having the requirement to deploy workload to multiple clusters.
Non-Goals * Provide a standard reference implementation. * Define specific implementation details beyond general API behavior.
